ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: After ignoring the curved arrows in the figure, a central carbon atom can be seen connected in four substituent directions: upper left connected to an R, lower left connected to an R, upward connected to OH2 and the oxonium part is marked with a positive charge, and lower right connected to a segment of carbon-carbon triple-bond chain, with the terminal of the triple bond connected to R1. Reasoning: Represent the generic substituents R and R1 both with the SMILES wildcard *. The main chain can be written as *C#CC according to R1–C≡C–C(center). The central carbon also has two other R branches, corresponding to (*)(*), and is connected to a positively charged hydrated hydroxyl substituent [OH2+]. Therefore the complete SMILES is *C#CC(*)(*)[OH2+].

method.method_draft: First describe the visual structure while ignoring the arrows: identify the main chain as R1–C≡C–C(center), where the central carbon also bears two R groups and an `[OH2+]` substituent. Convert each generic R/R1 endpoint to `*`, choose the alkynyl chain as `*C#CC`, then attach the two R branches and the oxonium branch to the terminal central carbon as `(*)(*)[OH2+]`, giving `*C#CC(*)(*)[OH2+]`.
